enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
1047 PM MDT Mon Oct 19 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 1100 PM MDT Mon Oct 19 2026

 - Isolated showers and thunderstorms expected for Tuesday, mainly
   limited to the high terrain and Southwest New Mexico.

 - Temperatures warming back up Tuesday and Wednesday, with
   lowland highs in the lower 80s. This is slightly above average
   for late October.

 - Widespread chances for showers and thunderstorms return
   Thursday and Friday as moisture moves north into the region.
   Some stronger storms could result in localized flooding.
   Flooding risk will be highest across western New Mexico and 
   the Gila Wilderness.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1100 PM MDT Mon Oct 19 2026

Diffluent southwest flow within the RE region of the subtropical
jet lead to isolated supercells and severe weather this evening.
00Z RAOB at KEPZ confirmed favorable wind shear and an increase in
moisture. Precipitable water is now 1.0-1.1" with 30-40 knots of
EBWS and a 45 knot speed max at 400mb, enough for some very strong
storms across SW NM today.

Prevailing weather pattern depicts a diving Pacific low moving
south down the California coast. This low will play a major role
in late-week rain chances for the El Paso area. To the south, high
pressure aloft is building over S TX and NE Mexico. SSW flow aloft
will continue to promote moisture advection out of the south,
leading to an extended period of rain chances for late-October.

For Tuesday temperatures will continue to warm a bit, reaching 
the lower 80s across most of the desert lowlands. Isolated showers
and thunderstorms are expected, again favoring SW NM and the high
terrain. Coverage will be lower, generally 10-20% given warmer 
air aloft eating away at instability. Still, favorable 0-6km wind
shear profiles could result in a couple strong to severe storms
across Grant/Hidalgo Counties. Very similar conditions on 
Wednesday, with scattered showers and thunderstorms favoring SW 
NM during the afternoon and evening hours.

Forecast remains on track for widespread rain chances
Thursday/Friday across Southern New Mexico and Far West Texas.
Pacific low will move ashore late this week, with a 75-knot jet
streak rounding the base of the system over the Southwest US.
Deep moisture flux out of Mexico will push precipitable water
values to 1.2-1.4", well above normal for this time of year.
Widespread showers and thunderstorms developing across E AZ and W
NM will slowly move east across the forecast area. Storms will be
capable of heavy rain and flash flooding. Current guidance put the
highest flood risk over W NM, including Grant County and the Gila
Wilderness (most likely rain amounts 1.00-1.50", worse-case 
2.00-3.00" localized). 

Models continue to struggle with the evolution of this system,
leaving remnant energy behind and continuing rain chances into 
the upcoming weekend. This comes at fairly low confidence right 
now, given the weaker forcing. This, however, is something the
area should get used to given a winter outlook that suggests above
normal precipitation and more frequent Pacific storm systems.

&&

.AVIATION...
(06Z TAFS)
Issued at 1100 PM MDT Mon Oct 19 2026

Scattered TS moving across S NM tonight, with lingering -RA 
behind it at local TAFs sites through 12Z. VCSH mention included 
at KELP/KLRU for a few hours into Tuesday morning. Overnight 
conditions VMC with skies SCT-BKN100 and surface winds VRB03KT. 
Light SE flow tomorrow, with isolated TSRA limited to S NM 
mountains. Not expecting TS mention in any local TAFs tomorrow.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1100 AM MDT Mon Oct 19 2026

While temperatures will be warming up the next couple of days to 
about 10 degrees above normal, fairly high moisture for Oct will 
be in place and keep RH's above 30%. There will be scattered 
thunderstorms almost daily, especially in area mountains going 
into the weekend. Best rain chances come Thu-Fri when some locally
heavy rainfall is possible, especially in the Gila region. 
Temperatures will be cooling down as we head into the later part 
of the week and rain chances increase. Vent rates generally Fair 
to good through Wed.
